newsitem.title: UK: Three British mums for twins born 22 months apart.
newsitem.headline: Three British mums for twins born 22 months apart.

text.p: A British woman was on Saturday celebrating the birth of a baby boy born 22 months after his twin sister in a surrogacy arrangement which gives the children three mothers.
The twin embryos were conceived in a test tube from the same batch of eggs collected from Tricia Gunther, 41, who spent 14 years trying to have a baby by fertility treatment herself.
Gunther and her husband Julian told the Daily Mail newspaper they found the first surrogate mother after advertising in a shop window. The woman, Teresa Finlay, gave birth in 1995 to baby Jennifer.
But Finlay was unwilling to go through another surrogate pregnancy to provide a brother or sister for Jennifer so the Gunthers found a second woman, Gaynor Crutchley, to carry the baby.
The baby boy was born on Thursday but has not been named yet.

"It's a miracle. I can't put into words the overwhelming emotion I feel. It is perfect. I now have a boy and a girl. The feling of holding your child and completing your family is just great," said Tricia Gunther.
British laws permit surrogacy arrangements providing neither party makes a commercial gain.
